indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B5.2.1.1 Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements
indicator.objective: Describe, orally or in writing, a given pattern, using mathematical language, such as one more, one less, five more, one more than or less than twice, etc.

skills.description: Use mathematical language to describe a pattern (e.g., “add 3”, “double”, “one more than”).
Write a description of a pattern.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Describing the numbers instead of the rule.
Using informal language that is imprecise.
Missing the starting point of the pattern.

questions.stem: Which phrase best describes the pattern 5, 10, 15, 20?
hints: What do you add to 5 to get 10?
questions.explanation: The pattern increases by 5 each time. The rule is “add 5”.
questions.misconception: Saying “add 10” because 10 appears in the pattern.

questions.stem: Which phrase best describes the pattern 2, 4, 6, 8?
questions.explanation: The pattern increases by 2 each time. The rule is “add 2”.

questions.stem: Describe the pattern 3, 6, 9, 12 in words.
hints: Look at the difference between numbers.
questions.explanation: The pattern starts at 3 and adds 3 each time. It is “add 3” or “skip count by 3”.

criteria.description: States the rule is “add 3” or “skip count by 3”.

questions.misconception: Describing only the numbers without the rule.

questions.stem: The pattern 10, 20, 30, 40 increases by ___ each time.
questions.explanation: The pattern increases by 10 each time.

questions.stem: Orally describe the pattern 1, 3, 5, 7.
hints: Say what you add each time.
questions.explanation: The learner should say the pattern increases by 2 each time, or that it is the odd numbers.

questions.stem: Which phrase best describes the pattern 100, 90, 80, 70?
questions.explanation: The pattern decreases by 10 each time. The rule is “subtract 10”.
questions.misconception: Saying “increases by 10” because the numbers are large.

questions.stem: Write a sentence describing the pattern 2, 4, 8, 16.
questions.explanation: Each number is double the previous number. The rule is “multiply by 2” or “double”.

criteria.description: States the rule is “multiply by 2” or “double”.

questions.stem: The pattern 5, 10, 15, 20 is skip counting by ___.
hints: What number is added each time?
questions.explanation: The pattern is skip counting by 5.

questions.stem: Orally describe the pattern of shapes: square, triangle, square, triangle, square.
questions.explanation: The learner should say the pattern repeats square, triangle.

criteria.description: States the repeating unit is square, triangle.

questions.stem: Write a sentence describing the pattern 20, 18, 16, 14.
questions.explanation: The pattern decreases by 2 each time. The rule is “subtract 2”.

questions.stem: Which mathematical term describes the pattern 1, 4, 9, 16?
questions.explanation: These are square numbers.

questions.stem: Orally describe the pattern 2, 5, 8, 11.
questions.explanation: The learner should say the pattern increases by 3 each time.

questions.stem: Which phrase best describes the pattern 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8?
options: Each term is the sum of the two previous terms
Each term is double the previous term
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two previous terms (Fibonacci pattern).

questions.stem: Describe the pattern 2, 6, 18, 54 using mathematical language.
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 3. The rule is “multiply by 3”.

questions.stem: Orally describe the pattern 100, 95, 90, 85.
questions.explanation: The learner should say the pattern decreases by 5 each time.

questions.stem: The pattern 3, 7, 11, 15 increases by ___ each time.
questions.explanation: The pattern increases by 4 each time.

questions.stem: Explain the rule for the pattern 1, 3, 6, 10, 15.
questions.explanation: The differences increase by 1 each time. These are triangular numbers. Each term adds one more than the previous addition.

criteria.description: Mentions the differences increase by 1 each time.
Identifies the pattern as triangular numbers.

questions.stem: Orally describe the pattern 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 and explain why.
questions.explanation: The learner should say these are square numbers and explain that each term is a number multiplied by itself.

criteria.description: Identifies the pattern as square numbers.
Explains each term is n × n.

questions.misconception: Saying it adds 3, then 5, then 7 without recognizing squares.

questions.stem: Describe a real-life pattern you have seen (e.g., in a kente design or a market display) and state its rule.
hints: Think of repeating colours or shapes.
questions.explanation: For example, a kente pattern may repeat red, yellow, blue, red, yellow, blue. The rule is the repeating unit red, yellow, blue.
questions.misconception: Describing a pattern without stating the rule.

questions.stem: Which phrase best describes the pattern 1, 2, 4, 8, 16?
questions.explanation: Each number doubles the previous number. The rule is “multiply by 2” or “double”.
